name: cycles have no startup order
input: a graph with a three-node directed dependency cycle
test:
has_cycle, order, reachability, impacts = analyze_topology(4, [(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 1)], [], [])
assert has_cycle is True
assert order == []
assert reachability == []
assert impacts == []

name: topological output places prerequisites before every dependent
input: an acyclic dependency graph with multiple roots
test:
edges = [(0, 2), (0, 3), (2, 1), (3, 1), (1, 4), (4, 5)]
has_cycle, order, reachability, impacts = analyze_topology(6, edges, [(0, 5), (2, 3), (0, 0)], [[1], [0, 0]])
assert has_cycle is False
assert set(order) == set(range(6))
position = {node: index for index, node in enumerate(order)}
assert all(position[dependency] < position[dependent] for dependent, dependency in edges)
assert reachability == [True, False, True]
assert impacts == [4, 1]

name: reverse failures do not travel from a dependent to its prerequisite
input: two independent machines that depend on one shared prerequisite
test:
has_cycle, order, reachability, impacts = analyze_topology(3, [(0, 1), (2, 1)], [(0, 1), (1, 0)], [[0], [1]])
assert has_cycle is False
assert set(order) == {0, 1, 2}
assert reachability == [True, False]
assert impacts == [1, 3]

name: single machines and parallel edges retain the stated semantics
input: an isolated machine plus repeated dependencies
test:
assert analyze_topology(1, [], [(0, 0)], [[0]]) == (False, [0], [True], [1])
has_cycle, order, reachability, impacts = analyze_topology(2, [(0, 1), (0, 1)], [], [[1]])
assert has_cycle is False
assert order == [1, 0]
assert impacts == [2]
